tasks.title: Pie charts: sources of electricity
tasks.prompt:
The pie charts below show the sources of electricity generated in one country in 2000 and 2020.

Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant.

visual.title: Sources of electricity generation
visual.note: Fictional data created for practice purposes.

examinerNotes: Overview should note: coal fell from the main source to a much smaller share; natural gas became the largest source; wind and solar grew strongly.
tasks.modelAnswer:
The two pie charts compare the sources used to generate electricity in one country in 2000 and 2020.

Overall, the country became much less dependent on coal over the twenty-year period, and natural gas replaced it as the main source. At the same time, wind and solar power grew from very small shares to significant ones, while nuclear and hydroelectric power changed very little.

In 2000, coal was by far the most important source, producing almost half (46%) of the country's electricity. Natural gas was second with 24%, followed by nuclear power (15%) and hydroelectric power (12%). Wind and solar energy together accounted for only 3% of the total.

By 2020, the share of coal had fallen dramatically to 18%, less than half its earlier level, while natural gas had risen to 31%, making it the largest single source. The most striking change, however, was the growth of renewable energy: wind power increased from 2% to 17% and solar power from 1% to 10%, so that together they produced more than a quarter of the country's electricity. Meanwhile, nuclear and hydroelectric power fell slightly, to 13% and 11% respectively.

tasks.title: Causes and solutions essay: household rubbish
tasks.prompt:
Write about the following topic:

In many cities, the amount of rubbish that people throw away is increasing every year.

What are the causes of this problem? What measures could be taken to reduce the amount of rubbish?

Give reasons for your answer and include any relevant examples from your own knowledge or experience.
tasks.modelAnswer:
Many cities are struggling with growing mountains of household waste, which fill landfill sites and pollute the environment. This essay will explain why people are throwing away more than in the past and suggest some practical ways to reduce the problem.

One major cause is the way products are sold today. Food, clothes and electronic goods are often wrapped in several layers of plastic and cardboard, and online shopping has made this worse, because every small order arrives in its own box. A second cause is the culture of convenience. Busy people buy ready meals, takeaway coffee and bottled water, all of which come in single-use containers. Finally, many goods are now cheap and designed to last only a short time, so people replace phones, furniture and clothing instead of repairing them.

Several measures could reduce the amount of waste. Firstly, governments could make manufacturers responsible for their packaging, for example by taxing excessive plastic or requiring companies to collect and recycle it. This would encourage businesses to use less material. Secondly, cities can make recycling and composting easy by providing separate bins for every household and charging people according to how much non-recyclable waste they produce. In places where this system has been introduced, waste levels have fallen significantly. Thirdly, individuals can change their habits by carrying reusable bags and bottles, buying second-hand goods and repairing items rather than throwing them away. Schools and media campaigns can play an important role in promoting these habits.

In conclusion, the rise in household rubbish is mainly the result of excessive packaging, convenience products and a throwaway culture. A combination of government regulation, better local services and changes in personal behaviour offers the best chance of reducing it.
